standards.name: MIxS (Minimum Information about any (x) Sequence)
standards.abstract: MIxS (Minimum Information about any (x) Sequence) is a metadata standard for contextual information about sequenced samples and the data derived from them. It covers a wide range of sequence-derived research objects (genomes, metagenomes, marker genes, metagenome-assembled genomes, uncultivated viruses, etc.) collected from diverse environments or hosts and recorded as structured metadata (LinkML/JSON/YAML) accompanying sequence data. The standard is maintained by the Genomic Standards Consortium (GSC) and published via a GitHub repository and a w3id; it provides checklists (called checklists or checklists+extensions/combinations) and environmental extensions that enumerate named metadata fields, their expected value types, structured patterns, and controlled vocabularies to improve discoverability and interoperability of sequence datasets.

classification.rationale: The source presents MIxS as a schema / term table (LinkML-generated documentation and a 'Full term table') where each named slot/term has a concrete range/type, cardinality, structured pattern or expected value. Individual term pages list 'Range', 'Cardinality', examples and structured patterns (i.e. genuine field-level metadata definitions). Example evidence: "MIxS, the Minimum Information about any (x) Sequence, is a standard from the Genomic Standards Consortium (GSC, https://www.gensc.org/) for reporting contextual metadata about sequenced samples."

standards.name: MIMS (Metagenome or Environmental)
standards.abstract: This checklist describes metadata fields for metagenome or environmental samples and associated sequencing/assembly data. The research objects are material/environmental samples and derived metagenomic sequence assemblies, collected under field or laboratory sampling conditions; recorded metadata include sample identifiers, geographic and environmental context, sample processing, sequencing and assembly methods, and related project details. The standard is presented as the MIxS (MIXS) 'MIMS' checklist (from the MIXS schema at https://w3id.org/mixs) and provides a structured list of named metadata slots with cardinality, data type, and textual descriptions to support consistent reporting and submission of metagenomic/environmental sample metadata.

classification.rationale: The source material is a checklist presented as a table of named metadata slots (MIXS identifiers) with explicit cardinality, data type and short descriptions for each slot, i.e. a genuine metadata table rather than prose guidance or ordered workflow.

standards.name: MIGS/MIMS (Minimum Information about a Genome/Metagenome Sequence) checklist (2010)
standards.abstract: The MIGS/MIMS checklist defines metadata fields for genome and metagenome sequence submissions and associated samples. It covers information about the investigation (project name, investigation type), experimental variables, geographic and environmental context (latitude/longitude, country/region, collection date, biome, feature, material), and submission/packaging details. The source material is a structured Excel checklist (MIGS_MIMS sheet) produced by the Genomic Standards Consortium (GSC) as part of the MIXS legacy; it lists each checklist item with a definition, examples, expected values, value syntax, and applicability (mandatory/optional) per checklist type. The standard addresses the problem of harmonizing minimal metadata required for sequence and environmental sample reporting to repositories (e.g., INSDC archives) and provides concrete syntaxes and controlled vocabularies (ISO 8601 for dates, EnvO, EFO/OBI terms, INSDC country list) to ensure consistent reporting.

classification.rationale: The source is an explicit spreadsheet checklist (columns: structured comment name, item, definition, example, expected value, value syntax, occurrence, etc.). Each row names a metadata field and provides a concrete value syntax or controlled vocabulary. This is a genuine metadata table rather than prose guidance or an ordered process.

standards.name: MIMARKS (Minimum Information about a Marker Sequence)
standards.abstract: MIMARKS defines a metadata checklist for marker-gene sequence data and related samples (e.g., surveys, isolates and cultures). The research objects are primarily nucleic-acid-based sequence records and their associated samples/environments; metadata are captured as structured checklist fields (geographic location, collection date, project/investigation descriptors, ontology-backed experimental factors, etc.). The source is an Excel workbook published as part of the Genomic Standards Consortium/MIGS/MIMS/MIMARKS legacy materials; it provides a worksheet of named structured-comment fields, human-readable definitions, example values, expected value syntax, and occurrence/requirement flags to support submission to INSDC archives (GenBank/ENA/DDBJ) and related repositories. The standard addresses minimum metadata required to make marker sequence records interpretable and reusable across environments (with additional environment-specific "packages" provided as subtables).

classification.rationale: The source is an explicit spreadsheet worksheet (MIMARKS sheet) that lists named fields (structured comment name / Item) together with concrete value syntax, examples, expected values, and occurrence -- i.e. a genuine metadata table rather than prose guidance or a procedural DAG.
